rule: Names are one grammar: place + function (dungeon with floor suffix, tower, castle, town). Hostile families take a corruption tier word in front of one base name (Cursed, Contaminated, Polluted), and the same tier word carries onto the drop item name. Elemental families are one base plus a six-element suffix. Faction presence is the guard NPC named by town or castle. Signs are client-text pointers in this half, so the sign grammar is only the object list and the notice-board types. Quest ladders are level-gated (15, 30, 45, 50) and step through givers with step numbers; a three-beat ladder is the shape of a short zone story. NPC shouts are timed rows with an interval and repeat flag, not sentences in the box.
keep: Corruption tier word on the creature name and on its drop name, from one data field
Zone name as place + function, floor suffix for vertical dungeons
Faction read from the guard name by town or castle
Notice board and sign as separate world objects with one-line content
Quest ladder as level-gated steps with named givers, each step one exchange
Ambient NPC line as a timed shout with an interval, not a sentence store
change: Use our own tier words, not the donor words
Use our own element set and our own base families
Castle war cadence set by our world, not the donor 2008 dates
No client string ids: our text lives in our data files
Leader-name handle fields are not carried over
Quest steps and town names are ours; only the step-ladder shape is kept
look_test: On a 375-wide phone, show one creature family at tier 0, 1 and 2 with the tier word in front of the name and the drop name carrying the same tier. Dom checks that the tier reads from the first word in under two seconds and that the zone entrance card (place + function + floor suffix) reads as a place, not a menu label.
